title: bug: profileRollout S1 pins the retained-id sort only through filesystem readdir order
description: strictRetention's `list.sort()` (state/profileRollout.ts:112) is pinned only by S1 (profileRollout.test.ts:260-286). S1 loads its tasks through an unsorted readdirSync (state/persistence.ts:42). On NTFS that order already equals the sorted order (task-S- before task-s00), so deleting `.sort()` survives there; on ext4 it depends on hash order. Add a test that feeds ids in a known non-sorted order, independent of the filesystem, and asserts the sorted, capped lists (QA comment-8e9714d3 on task-ced85748, found in the CQ-M06 epic review).
definitionOfDone: A test fails when `.sort()` is removed from strictRetention's ids() regardless of directory listing order, and passes with it
No production code change; cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/profileRollout.test.ts exits 0

implementationPlan.description:
Add test S3 at the end of the 'rollback retention' describe in profileRollout.test.ts (after S2), and add `strictRetention` to the existing import from './profileRollout.js' (line 18). Edit with the Edit tool only (global rail: TOOL witness). Test-only change: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/profileRollout.ts must stay byte-identical (DoD 2).

Design (independent of the filesystem by construction):
1. Ids, ascending by construction: `const r = (i: number) => String(i).padStart(2, '0'); const TASKS = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_v, i) => `task-r${r(i)}`); const ATTEMPTS = TASKS.map((id) => id.replace('task-', 'attempt-'));`. The zero padding keeps code-unit order equal to numeric order.
2. `await seed(TASKS.map((id) => ({ id, status: 'WORKING', planRevision: 3, executionPolicySnapshot: STRICT })));` Default settings are enough, because strictRetention never reads settings.
3. Open one strict attempt per task, with an explicit id, awaiting each call in turn: `await openAttempt(h.state, { id: ATTEMPTS[i], taskId: TASKS[i], workerId: 'worker-r', runnerId: 'runner-r', workspace: h.testDir, executionPolicySnapshot: STRICT } as never)`. Explicit attempt ids already appear in delivery/requiredChecks.test.ts:236 and state/attemptStore.test.ts:100. openAttempt refuses only a second open attempt on the SAME task.
4. Put the loaded tasks back into the SAME Map in descending id order, whatever readdirSync returned at load: `const descending = [...h.state.tasks].sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? 1 : -1)); h.state.tasks.clear(); for (const [id, task] of descending) h.state.tasks.set(id, task);`. Never assign a new Map to h.state.tasks. Then assert the precondition `expect([...h.state.tasks.keys()]).toEqual([...TASKS].reverse());`. This assertion is what makes the test independent of directory listing order. Above this block, add one short comment on why: loadEntities inserts in readdirSync order, and NTFS already returns S1's ids sorted.
5. `expect(strictRetention(h.state)).toEqual({ retainedStrictTasks: 12, retainedStrictTaskIds: TASKS.slice(0, 10), retainedStrictAttempts: 12, retainedStrictAttemptIds: ATTEMPTS.slice(0, 10), unreadableSnapshots: 0 });`. The expected lists are the literal ascending ids. NEVER build them by re-sorting the actual output: that oracle would pass the mutant.

Why this kills the mutants: the Map iterates r11..r00. Without .sort(), both lists come out r11..r02. If the sort runs after the cap, they come out r02..r11. Only sort-then-cap gives r00..r09. Twelve ids, more than MAX_RECORDED_IDS (10), also pin the attempt-list cap, which S1 (one strict attempt) does not.

Error handling: the test adds no try/catch. A task that fails to load, or a throw that strictRetention swallows, shows up as a visible diff (a count other than 12, or unreadableSnapshots other than 0), never as a silent pass. Leave S1, S2 and every other test unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Stubbing fs.readdirSync during load was rejected: one readdirSync serves every entity directory, so a stub is fragile and the test would still be shaped by the filesystem. (2) A fake StateManager object passed to strictRetention was rejected: it couples the test to which state fields strictRetention and currentAttempt read, and a missing field turns into a swallowed throw counted as unreadable. (3) The hand-off in comment 8e9714d3 on task-ced85748 suggested random attempt ids plus 'a few attempts'. That was replaced with explicit ids, because openAttempt accepts an id, which makes the order fully deterministic instead of probabilistic. (4) Driving it through update({executionProfile:'legacy'}) and reading the activity record is not needed: the record spreads strictRetention(state) verbatim, and S1 already pins that path. The direct call isolates the ordering contract.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: strictRetention (profileRollout.ts:94-120) pushes task ids, and each task's open-attempt id, in state.tasks insertion order. That order is loadEntities' readdirSync order (persistence.ts:38-55), so on NTFS S1's ids already arrive sorted and dropping .sort() survives. currentAttempt (attemptStore.ts:154) filters state.attempts by taskId, so the attempt push order follows the task iteration order. Explicit attempt ids have test precedent in delivery/requiredChecks.test.ts:236 and state/attemptStore.test.ts:100. The S1 const at the top of the test file is a session id, not a test; name the new test 'S3 ...' in its title only.
planningNotes.risks: Replacing h.state.tasks with a new Map, instead of clear+set, could desync any holder of the old reference. Dropping the precondition assertion would make the test silently depend on load order again. An expected list computed as [...actual].sort() would pass the mutant, so use literal ascending ids. Without zero-padding, code-unit order differs from numeric order. Mutants run only on the snapshot copy: restore from the pinned SHA, never a per-mutant backup. A transform error is a false kill. In-tree vitest fails under WSL (Windows-native node_modules), and the global rail forbids it anyway: gate in a snapshot only.
